pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: The center of gravity is located aft of the main gear pivot point
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: Forward momentum acts to continue and tighten a turn without further steering input
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: Removing rudder pressure ordinarily does not stop a turn once it has been started

pairs.answer: The tailwheel is located forward of the main gear

pairs.answer: The center of gravity is located ahead of the main gear
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: The aircraft lacks a rudder-pedal-operated steering mechanism
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: Braking action is insufficient to counteract forward momentum
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: The wide main gear track creates excessive pivot resistance
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: The tailwheel is fixed and cannot swivel during ground operations
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: Nose-heavy loading causes the aircraft to veer unpredictably
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: Why are tailwheel aircraft considered inherently unstable on the ground?
pairs.answer: The propeller torque overwhelms directional control at low speeds
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It returns the tailwheel to a center position when rudder pedal input is relaxed

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It assists pilots in regaining straight-line travel after a turn
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It compensates for the tailwheel's tendency to remain deflected after steering input ceases
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It locks the tailwheel in a fixed position during takeoff roll
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It automatically applies opposite rudder to stop an initiated turn
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It prevents the tailwheel from swiveling beyond a set angle
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It increases rudder pedal resistance to discourage abrupt steering inputs
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It connects the tailwheel directly to the rudder for improved response
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It dampens propeller torque effects during ground operations
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It ensures the tailwheel remains aligned with the main gear at all times
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the purpose of a centering spring or similar device on a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: It replaces differential braking as the primary directional control method
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.answer: Apply rudder pressure to initiate the turn

pairs.question: What is the correct rudder technique for making a taxi turn in a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: Increase engine power to counteract the tightening tendency during turns
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the correct rudder technique for making a taxi turn in a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: Use nose-wheel steering techniques identical to those used in tricycle-gear aircraft
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 14, Section 14.2 – Instability

pairs.question: What is the correct rudder technique for making a taxi turn in a tailwheel airplane?
pairs.answer: Apply rudder only after the desired heading is reached to stop the turn

pairs.answer: Hold rudder pressure until the aircraft has fully stopped before neutralizing
